comparison: Both evaluate plasma biochemistry claims (C4, C5, C26-C30). OpenEval finds the data well-supported with appropriate statistics and adequate sample sizes. Peer reviewers acknowledge therapeutic effects but rate as UNCERTAIN, noting critical limitations: lack of liver histology and insufficient evaluation beyond plasma markers to fully support therapeutic efficacy claims.

Both address metabolic modeling claims (C63-C64). OpenEval finds Compass analysis well-supported with appropriate statistics but notes validation with metabolomic data would strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, explicitly critiquing reliance on computational predictions without direct metabolite measurements, creating uncertainty about metabolic modeling conclusions.

Both address background/contextual claims (C1-C3, C12-C21, C59-C62, C65-C66, with peer also including C53). Both evaluations agree these represent established knowledge appropriately cited. OpenEval notes they are not novel findings; peer reviewers accept without challenge as established context.

Both evaluate safety/toxicity claims (C22-C25), with peer also including behavioral safety (C31). Both find the data supported. OpenEval notes adequate preliminary toxicology despite small sample sizes. Peer reviewers accept safety findings without challenge, noting effective assessment of side effects for clinical application.

Both address skeletal muscle transcriptomic findings (C10, C45-C48, C57, C44, C9). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the striking finding that 97-99% of DEGs are treatment-specific and notes immune pathway upregulation requires further investigation. Peer reviewers accept as novel and important, part of solid conclusions about multi-tissue metabolism.

Both evaluate liver/adipose transcriptomic claims (C6-C7, C37-C39, C52), with peer also covering C8, C40-C43, C54-C56. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds comprehensive analysis with appropriate statistics and pathway enrichment. Peer reviewers strongly affirm as central contributions with solid conclusions supported by experimental and modeling approaches.

Both address differential expression and pathway claims (C8, C40-C43, C56), with peer covering broader transcriptomic findings (C6-C7, C37-C39, C52, C54-C55). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights significant overlaps and pathway enrichment. Peer reviewers affirm as solid central contributions with robust systems biology approaches.

Both evaluate inter-tissue coordination claims (C49-C51, C58), with peer also covering C11, C68-C70. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds correlation analysis supports inter-tissue coordination but mechanism remains speculative. Peer reviewers strongly support as key contribution demonstrating drug effects are more widespread than specific tissues, emphasizing tissue interaction importance.

Both address gene expression claims (C34-C35), with OpenEval also covering C32-C33 and peer including C36. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds RNA-seq data with appropriate statistics and tissue-specific patterns align with known biology. Peer reviewers accept molecular findings without question as supporting inter-tissue metabolic coordination.

Both evaluate co-expression network claims (C68-C70), with peer also covering broader inter-tissue findings (C11, C49-C51, C58). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds network analysis provides mechanistic insight into inter-tissue communication with moderate but significant correlations. Peer reviewers strongly affirm as solid conclusions supported by experimental and modeling approaches.

Both address correlation between plasma TG and skeletal muscle JNK2 (C36). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes correlation suggests mechanistic link but causality cannot be inferred. Peer reviewers accept without question as supporting evidence for inter-tissue metabolic coordination.

Both evaluate skeletal muscle minimal response to sucrose (C9, C44). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval documents tissue-specific response pattern contrasting with liver/adipose. Peer reviewers accept as part of novel and important findings about multi-tissue metabolism.

Both address behavioral safety (C31). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes multiple behavioral assays show no significant differences, addressing important safety concern, though detailed statistics not in main text. Peer reviewers accept without challenge, noting effective assessment of side effects.

Both evaluate the key conceptual conclusion about inter-tissue metabolic coordination (C11). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds it supported by comprehensive multi-tissue analysis showing substantial changes and inter-tissue correlations. Peer reviewers strongly affirm as demonstrating drug effects are more widespread than specific tissues, emphasizing tissue interaction importance.

OpenEval addresses tissue-specific regulation patterns (C53-C55) rating as SUPPORTED with literature context. Peer R2 covers broader transcriptomic findings including C54-C55 as part of central contributions rated SUPPORTED. Both affirm the tissue-specific differential expression findings.
OpenEval evaluates methodological scope claim (C67) as SUPPORTED, noting it represents standard RNA-seq practice. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological statement.
